records.reason: m107 at 5/1 and 150 ul tests a high-loading response point in a predicted late carbonyl-rich regime and can improve both endpoint heads.
The same m107 ratio and loading solvent at 100 ul adds a sample-volume contrast that can separate amount effects from the predicted broad finish.
m107 at 2/1 and 150 ul extends the molecule-specific ratio curve below the selected 5/1 point and constrains local interpolation.
The 1/1 m107 point anchors the lower-strength side of the predicted response and helps prevent a global solvent correction from absorbing molecule-specific curvature.
m125 at 1/1 with 50 ul sample and 500 ul DCM probes the loading-solvent-volume dimension at a lower ratio, providing a surface anchor for amount and volume effects.
m125 at 2/1 and 150 ul with 500 ul DCM gives a higher-amount comparison to other selected m125 rows while retaining the same loading-solvent volume.
m125 at 2/1 and 100 ul with 300 ul DCM adds the lower-volume side of the proposed loading surface and helps distinguish solvent volume from sample amount.
m125 at 5/1 and 150 ul supplies a high-ratio, higher-loading point for testing whether loading changes onset and finish differently in a late predicted regime.
m207 at 2/1 and 50 ul fills a predicted interior ratio location where a steep local response could otherwise be interpolated incorrectly.
The 0/1 m207 point at 150 ul tests predicted loading transfer at the weak-eluent boundary and anchors the low-strength side of the curve.
m207 at 5/1 and 150 ul is a higher-loading point in the predicted steep region and can test whether the large onset shift transfers with loading.
m207 at 10/1 and 100 ul tests the upper part of the predicted local response while changing sample volume, informing both ratio curvature and loading interaction.
m117 at 20/1 and 150 ul extends the predicted fixed-loading ratio curve toward a late regime and supplies finish-head supervision.
The 50/1 m117 point tests the predicted high-ratio tail at the same nominal sample volume as the 20/1 point, helping distinguish ratio curvature from loading effects.
m94 at 20/1 and 100 ul targets a broad predicted finish and adds a loading contrast in a carbonyl-rich molecule where V2 may need separate calibration.
m94 at 10/1 and 50 ul supplies an interior ratio point between predicted early and late regimes, constraining interpolation of both heads.
m181 at 10/1 and 50 ul tests the predicted loading response near an interior ratio in a cyclic ester and can repair local onset interpolation.
m181 at 20/1 and 50 ul probes whether the predicted late finish remains loading-sensitive after the ratio response becomes strong.
m179 at 2/1 and 100 ul samples the lower-ratio side of a predicted fused-ketone response and improves local structural transfer for the ring system.
m180 at 5/1 and 100 ul bridges predicted moderate and weak-eluent regimes for a related fused ketone, testing whether its response is gradual or localized.
m180 at 20/1 and 100 ul extends the same loading condition into a high-ratio regime and can improve upper-tail extrapolation for the scaffold.
m63 at 20/1 and 100 ul provides a substituted fused-ketone comparator under matched nominal conditions, testing graph-specific effects on response slope.
m6 at 10/1 and 100 ul adds an interior ratio point for a cyclic-acetal aromatic environment and tests whether its predicted curve is flatter than related oxygen systems.
m8 at 20/1 and 50 ul extends the fused-furan response into a late ratio and helps distinguish oxygen topology from generic polarity transfer.
m122 at 5/1 and 100 ul supplies a lower-ratio anchor for a positional dimethoxy-bromobenzene response and tests local structural interpolation.
m122 at 20/1 and 100 ul adds a high-ratio point for the same sparse oxygen-rich environment, improving finish-tail transfer across related rows.
m36 at 1/1 and 100 ul is a loading contrast for a conjugated amino ketone and tests whether its predicted early response is amount-sensitive.
m36 at 2/1 and 150 ul combines a stronger ratio with higher loading, testing interaction between amino-ketone retention and sample amount.
m128 at 0/1 and 100 ul anchors the low-strength side of a thioether aromatic ketone response and improves local graph-specific interpolation.
m128 at 2/1 and 100 ul adds an interior ratio point before the predicted stronger response, constraining both endpoint heads.
m173 at 10/1 with 100 ul sample and 1500 ul DCM tests a predicted acid-containing late response while holding the unusual loading-solvent volume explicit.
m200 at 2/1 and 150 ul samples a polar nitro-alcohol environment with a broad predicted interval, adding transfer information for finish-tail behavior.

hypotheses.content: PE/EA response is often steep and structure-specific, with V1 and V2 changing at different rates; local intermediate labels are more informative than a global monotonic solvent correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Interior ratio labels constrain response shape and reduce interpolation errors in molecule-condition regions where the two endpoint heads may curve differently.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected interior points show smooth response, localized transitions, or head-specific curvature?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent volume interact with molecule and PE/EA ratio, and their effects on V1 and V2 need not have the same direction or magnitude.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts can teach interactions currently suppressed by nearly invariant predictions and improve transfer to unseen loading conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which loading effects transfer within a molecule across ratios, and which depend on the retention regime?

hypotheses.content: For m125, sample amount and loading-solvent volume form a two-factor response surface with potentially separate effects on onset and finish.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A small local m125 design can distinguish amount, solvent-volume and interaction terms instead of allowing confounded loading effects to generalize incorrectly.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m125 labels form a consistent surface over amount and loading-solvent volume for each endpoint?

hypotheses.content: Close structural analogies and aggregate polarity descriptors may not transfer PE/EA response shape; ring environment, substitution and heteroatom topology may require graph-level discrimination.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related fused ketones, oxygen-rich aromatics and amino ketones provide structured positive and negative transfer examples for molecular representation learning.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do related scaffolds share response slopes after nominal loading is accounted for, or do local graph features dominate?

hypotheses.content: V2 finish tails can vary independently of V1 in polar, carbonyl-rich, acid-containing and nitro-functional molecules, so upper-tail supervision is needed alongside onset repair.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Late and broad conditions can improve calibration of the finish head without assuming that V1 and V2 share one error mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural and loading features predict a broad finish after onset has been constrained?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback strengthened the need for matched loading and local response-curve experiments. The m125 outcomes indicate that sample amount and loading-solvent volume should be separated explicitly. The m207 outcomes motivate more interior ratio and loading points around a steep response. The fused-ketone and oxygen-rich aromatic outcomes weaken simple analogical transfer and favor graph-specific local repairs. The m117 outcome weakens the proposed nonmonotonic interpolation interpretation and supports testing its increasing ratio curve. The selected batch therefore emphasizes molecule-specific response surfaces, with additional V2-focused points for broad predicted tails.
batch_rationale: The batch combines exact loading contrasts, interior PE/EA response points, structural transfer tests and finish-tail supervision. The m107 and m125 groups address high-impact loading and late-response regions. The m207, m117, m94 and m181 groups constrain local solvent curves. Fused ketones, oxygen-rich aromatics, amino ketones and thioether ketones test whether related structures share response slopes. The acid and polar late-tail rows add coverage for endpoint asymmetry. Together these labels should improve generalization by teaching structure-condition interactions and separate V1/V2 behavior while retaining meaningful local redundancy.
